findings.body: With no sign-off pin, `approval.signed_off` treats any accepted decision whose name ends in `client-signoff.md` as sign-off (`src/forge/approval.py:104-112`). This new filter requires a four-digit prefix. A client with an accepted unpinned record such as `docs/decisions/customer-client-signoff.md` is therefore signed off to Forge's existing gate, but `forge merge` still gets the pre-sign-off `agent` setting and can merge despite `merge = "human"`. Use the same accepted-record rule at this boundary.
findings.title: Not done: Prototype changes merge themselves

findings.body: The new command test covers only an unpinned `0001-client-signoff.md`. It never sets `forge.toml`'s `signoff` pin, so an implementation that lets a different accepted decision restore human merge authority would pass every new case. Add a real `forge close`/`forge merge` case with a pinned record and a different accepted sign-off on the fetched default branch; only the pinned record should change the effective setting.
findings.title: Not done: pinned sign-off merge test

findings.body: The plan assigns this to TALK after MERGE. `src/forge/nextstep.py:304,317` still reads the raw `merge` value, so a ready pre-sign-off item configured for human merge tells the salesperson to merge it; its cleanup path also misses `forge merge`. The Forge skill at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:41-43` likewise tells the agent to use `forge merge` only when the raw setting is `agent`. TALK needs to update those paths and prove them through its assigned command test.
